description: The configuration package has two modules: defaults.py holds a module-level DEFAULTS dictionary including a nested 'headers' mapping, and settings.py merges caller overrides into it. load_settings() currently aliases DEFAULTS instead of copying it, so one call permanently changes the defaults seen by every later call, and nested dictionaries are shared. Fix settings.load_settings() so each call returns an independent deep copy and defaults.DEFAULTS is never modified. Do not change defaults.py.
expected_behavior: After load_settings({'timeout': 99}), defaults.DEFAULTS['timeout'] is still 30. Mutating the returned 'headers' does not affect DEFAULTS. Two calls are independent.
notes: Synthetic defect seeded for the VerifyLoop benchmark. Not a production incident.
title: Settings loader mutates shared defaults across modules
